content_metadata.description: This video provides a detailed analysis of the humerus bone, highlighting its various parts and their anatomical significance. The instructor uses a humerus bone model and forceps to illustrate key features.

qAndA.question: What bony landmark articulates with the glenoid cavity of the scapula?
What is the common name for the medial epicondyle?
Which projection is located on the lateral side of the distal humerus?
What groove is found between the greater and lesser tubercles?
What fossa is located on the posterior side of the distal humerus?

activities.description: Pointing to different parts of the bone with forceps

scenes.contextualRelevance: The instructor uses descriptive language and precise pointing to ensure clear understanding of the bone's complex features, contributing to the educational nature of the video.

text_to_speech: Okay so now we're looking at the humerus. Your upper arm bone there. Okay so starting at the top of it we have the head of the humerus, right here, it's what's articulating with the glenoid cavity of the scapula. Then we have a neck in the humerus this cases we technically have two necks so the neck is kind of where it begins to thin out from the head itself but with the way that the humerus is shaped we have a anatomical neck right at the base of the head here but we also have a surgical neck right here. Okay we've got the Greater and Lesser tubercles so the greater is kind of higher up on top here the lesser is kind of little further down, both sticking out projections there. The intertubercular sulcus or groove is in between them you can see the deltoid tuberosity kind of this rough part of the humerus. Going down towards the bottom here this is kind of be where your elbow would be, we have a medial epicondyle, okay so this is the large projection off to the side it's your funny bone is that part you hit and it hurts like crazy not so funny. okay and this of course on this side over here would make this our lateral epicondyle okay you can see this kind of hole right here okay this is the coronoid fossa and you have two projections here and here on the medial side is the trochlea on the lateral side is the capitulum, on the back side another hole here is the olecranon fossa
